newsitem.title: UK: BZW ups gilt weighting for first time in two years.
newsitem.headline: BZW ups gilt weighting for first time in two years.

text.p: British investment bank BZW said on Thursday it increased its weighting of gilts in its recommended bond portfolio to neutral from underweight for the first time in two years.
Mark Capleton, international bond strategist at BZW in London, said the increase was made for a number of reasons.
"The obvious one is the gilt market has not tightened to Germany when every other spread market has done well," he said.
Capleton added a victory by the opposition Labour party at the next general election has been fairly fully priced into gilt yields. Britain must hold an election by May 1997.
Opinion polls show the Labour party in the lead.
Capleton said Labour is expected to strive to meet the Maastricht criteria for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) whether it brought Britain into the union or not.
The criteria restrict public deficits to no more than three percent of GDP.
"That disciple remains in force," Capleton said.
He also said inflation rates in core European markets such as Germany and France are currently seen in the best light because they are behind Britain in the economic cycle.

"Although there is an inflation difference between the UK and core Europe, a sizable chunk of that will be purely cyclical," he said. "If you're investing in long-term instruments, you really have to look through the cycle," he said.

Technically, the gilt yield curve also looks better than two years ago when it discounted the gilt/Bund spread tightening dramatically. It has now normalised versus other European spreads, Capleton said.
BZW has a 12-month target of 125 basis points on the gilt/Bund 10-year yield spread, but Capleton said most of the gains will come after the election. The gap is currently at 177.
Capleton said at the same time, BZW has reduced its weighting of Spanish bonds to neutral from overweight after their recent outperformance.
The recommended weighting of BZW's bond portolio currently stands as follows:
Aggressively underweight -- Belgium, Japan, Ecu, France
Neutral -- U.S., Britian, Cananda, Australia, Spain
